text: justify Detection of non-overlapping and overlapping communities are essentially the same problem. However, current algorithms focus either on finding overlapping or non-overlapping communities. We present a generalized framework that can identify both non-overlapping and overlapping communities, without any prior input about the network or its community distribution. To do so, we introduce a vertex-based metric, GenPerm , that quantifies by how much a vertex belongs to each of its constituent communities. Our community detection algorithm is based on maximizing the GenPerm over all the vertices in the network. We demonstrate, through experiments over synthetic and real-world networks, that GenPerm is more effective than other metrics in evaluating community structure. Further, we show that due to its vertex-centric property, GenPerm can be used to unfold several inferences beyond community detection, such as core-periphery analysis and message spreading. Our algorithm for maximizing GenPerm outperforms six state-of-the-art algorithms in accurately predicting the ground-truth labels. Finally, we discuss the problem of resolution limit in overlapping communities and demonstrate that maximizing GenPerm can mitigate this problem.

Imagine that behind the speedometer, there's a small metal cup connected to the needle's shaft by its base, so the open end of the cup is facing away from you. This is called the speed cup. The magnet is positioned so it's inside the open end of this cup, but not touching it quite. Got that so far? Wheel, cable, magnet, and then around this magnet is a cup, which is connected to the needle. The'eddy currents' at the heart of all of this will (without going into the technicalities) try and make the cup turn with the magnet, and so make the needle turn with the magnet. Of course you don't want the speedo needle spinning like a clock from a horror movie, so there's a fairly weak spring that holds it at zero. The faster you go, the more force the magnet is putting into the speed cup to make it turn away from the zero point, and so the further round the needle will go, slow down and the spring will pull the needle back to zero again.
